To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intermittent exposure to short durations of hypoxia per episode (15 s of 0.5% O2 + 5 min normoxia) for 10 days resulted in a significant increase in the carotid sinus nerve activity in response to graded isoxcopic hypoxia, and the effect was completely reversed after 10 days of normoxia, suggesting that the carotid chemoreceptors were sensitized to hypoxia.
SDIH but no LDIH resulted in augmentation of hypoxic sensory response and that this was associated with increased O(2)(-) radical formation in carotid bodies.
chronic intermittent hypoxias that differ in the number of exposures per day and the duration of each episode of hypoxia differentially affect the hypoxic sensing function of the carotids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of chronic intermittent hypoxic exposure on carotid bodies, which are the main chemoreceptors in the cardiovascular control system, and the mechanisms underlying these effects.
the mechanisms by which intermittent hypoxia affects cardiorespiratory function in obstructive sleep apnea patients.

SDIH but LDIH does not augment the carotid sensory response to hypoxia and that the augmentation in hypoxic sensory responses in SDIH is mediated through O(2)(-) radicals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic intermittent hypoxias of short durations per day (SDI) are more potent than long durations per day (LDI) in sensitizing the hypoxic sensory activity of the carotids.
chronic intermittent hypoxias with different patterns of hypoxic exposures have distinct effects on the hypoxic sensing of the carotids.
SDIH results in selective augmentation in hypoxic response of carotid bodies by increasing the sensitivity of the O(2) sensor in carotid body glomus cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chronic intermittent hypoxias of different paradigms may have different effects on carotid bodies, which may have important implications in the pathogenesis of cardiorespiratory disorders.
the effects of CIH on the carotid chemosensory system are dependent on the duration and frequency of the exposures to hypoxia and may be mediated in part by reactive oxygen species.
the duration and frequency of intermittent hypoxic exposure play an important role for the carotid sensory response to intermittent hypoxia.
